text: Hello, boys and girls, welcome to Daisy's class.Today, we are going to start listening and speaking part one.In this period, you are going to listen to several conversations and get to know what they are talking about.Besides, you'll get the chance to use the target language in real situations.Please get your student's book and the worksheet ready.Look at the picture and make a guess about the man's job and what Lo is doing.Good, from what the man wears, we can see he is probably a shop assistant.Lo is probably talking about the CD.Listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.You can find it on your worksheet, task one.You will listen to the dialogue only once.Ready, go.So much for listening, let's check.What is Lo doing?Great, he is complaining about the CD.We can also say he is making a complaint about the CD.Here, complain, verb, complaint, noun.Read after me, complain, complaint.What does Lo think of the CD?He thinks the CD is broken because there is a hole in the middle.Can a shop assistant understand Lo?No, he gets confused.Think about the following questions.Look at the picture and think about the questions.The pepper is rotten.From the picture, we can easily get the meaning of rotten.The pepper is of very poor quality.It went bad.What if you buy a rotten pepper from the supermarket?Of course, you will make a complaint.What do you need to have when complaining?Yes, a piece of paper with items listed.We call it receipt.Pay attention to the pronunciation of the word.The letter P in the word is silent.Read after me, receipt, receipt.Please move on to task two on your worksheet.Alan goes to the supermarket to complain to David, the manager.Listen to the conversation and answer questions one and two.Yes, here it is.Thanks.Now, if you can wait, I'll be back in a moment.Okay, have you got the answers?Great, let's check.What did Alan complain about?Yes, two of the peppers she bought were rotten.What would David do?He will bring her some fresh peppers.Got it?Listen to the conversation again and answer questions three and four.The word apologize means say sorry.Read after me, apologize.Excuse me, I want to complain about these peppers.What's the problem?When I took off the plastic, I found that two of them were rotten.Look.Oh, I'm very sorry about that.I'll take care of it right away.Can you show me your receipt?So much for listening.What did Alan say to begin her complaint?Great.She said, I want to complain about these peppers.What did David say to apologize?Clear?Good.Let's move on.Here's the conversation you listened just now.Read the conversation after the recording and then think about the steps of making a complaint and how to respond to the complaint.Let's discover the steps together.Alan said, I want to complain about these peppers.I want to complain about these peppers.So first, express what you want to complain about.Second, explain why you complained as Alan did.What about David?How did he respond?David said, What's the problem?To express concern.Next, after listening to the complaint, he said sorry, apologized.And then, David will work out a solution to fix the problem.Two more questions for you to think about.How did Alan begin her complaint?Why did Alan begin her complaint in this way?What do you think?Did Alan begin her complaint rudely?She did it gently, politely.Although she felt angry, she still wanted the problem fixed.Remember, it's important to put focus onto solving problems rather than creating new ones.Now, let's get more practice.Please move on to task three on your worksheet.Kate is in Happy's pet shop.She is talking to the clock.Listen to the conversation and answer the questions.You'll hear the conversation twice.Read through the questions first and get ready.Excuse me.Yes, madam.How can I help you?I'm sorry, but I'd like to make a complaint about this dog.I bought him from you recently.Last Monday, in fact.What's wrong?He keeps barking at night, which not only stops us from sleeping, but also disturbs the neighbors.I'm very sorry about that.If you don't mind, just let him stay here to get some training until he behaves better.Thank you.That couldn't be better.Now, listen again.Alright, let's check what happened.What did Kate complain about?She complained about the dog she bought last Monday.What did Kate say to begin the complaint?She said, I'm sorry, but I'd like to make a complaint about this dog.Why did Kate complain?The dog kept barking all night.What would the clock do to fix Kate's problem?He would give the dog some training until the dog behaved better.The last one.Was Kate satisfied with the solution?Yes, she was.Have you got all the answers?If you missed out something, don't forget to take notes.Let's take a look at what we listened to just now.The steps of complaining and the way to respond to the complaint are almost the same as we learned just now.But with different expressions.Kate said, I'm sorry, but I'd like to make a complaint about this dog.She expressed what she wanted to complain very politely.The clock said, what's wrong?From the two conversations, we learned how to complain and how to respond to complaints.Now let's read the tips on how to complain and respond to complaints.Use indirect language to start your complaint, such as, I'm sorry, but I'd like to make a complaint about.Excuse me, I want to make a complaint about.Or, excuse me, I want to complain about.I'm not very happy about.Explain why you are upset or dissatisfied.Remember, keep your voice calm.When responding to complaints, express concern.What's the trouble?Listen to the customer's experience patiently.Apologize.I'm terribly or very sorry about that.I'm sorry to hear that.Try to work out a satisfying solution.Remember, always wear a smile.Okay, it's time for you to practice on your own.Choose one of the situations to make a conversation in pairs by using the structure and expressions you've just learned.You've got two minutes to practice.Now, let's listen to Yoyo and Bart.Excuse me, I have a complaint about this rice.When I opened the bag, I found that there were bugs in it.Oh, I'm terribly sorry about that.Can you give me your receipt?Yes, here you are.Thanks, just a minute.I'll get you another bag of fine rice.Excellent.One more pair, Anna and Annie.Excuse me, I want to complain about this soya milk.When I opened the carton, I found that it was a funny color.Can you fix it?Oh, I'm awfully sorry about that.Can I have your receipt?Thanks, now if you can wait, I'll be back in a second.Good job.Today's homework.This is the end of today's class.See you next time.
